bull_case: AI gets commoditized at the model layer, which favors Adobe's distribution and workflow ownership.
bear_case: If agentic tools bypass Adobe file/workflow standards, switching costs can erode quickly.
thesis: The moat is under pressure at the model layer but remains resilient at the workflow/ecosystem layer. Adobe's best defense is not having the best standalone model; it is making AI a feature across a deeply embedded creative/document/marketing stack.

evidence.claim: AI-first ARR grew >150% y/y, indicating AI is being absorbed into the ecosystem.

counterevidence: AI lowers content-creation barriers and could shift value from application vendors toward models, distribution layers or new agentic workflows.
unknowns: Long-run AI monetization per user, Firefly inference economics, and how much AI-first ARR is incremental versus bundled/reclassified ARR.
falsifiers: If ARR growth falls to low single digits while AI usage rises, or owner FCF/share stops compounding despite buybacks, the moat/compounder thesis is downgraded.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: ARR, subscription revenue, usage and AI monetization do not show persistent moat shrinkage.

next_checks: Q4/FY2026 ARR, AI-first ARR, OCF, SBC, repurchases, share count and Digital Media/Experience growth

subscores.rationale: Workflow depth, file formats, skills and enterprise integrations still create meaningful switching costs.
Installed base, assets, templates, enterprise data and app integrations reinforce ecosystem value.
Adobe can bundle third-party models and Firefly inside workflows, reducing dependence on model-level differentiation.

uncertainties.rationale: AI monetization and competitive workflow migration remain the central uncertainty.
